questions.question: What is the area of a triangle whose sides measure 5 cm, 6 cm and 7 cm?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The side of the triangle is 5, 6 and 7 cm 

**Formula Used:**

Area of triangle = √[s(s - a)(s - b)(s-c)], where s = semiperimeter of the triangle 

Semiperimeter (S) = (1/2) × Sum of sides of the triangle

**Calculation:**

Semiperimeter (s) = (a + b + c)/2 = (5 + 6 + 7)/2 = 9

⇒ Area of the triangle = √[s(s - a)(s - b)(s-c)]

⇒ √[9(9 - 5)(9 - 6)(9 - 7)] = √(9 × 4 × 3 × 2) = 14.69 cm² 

**∴ the area of the triangle is 14.69 cm2**

questions.question: What is the length (in cm) of the smallest altitude of the triangle whose sides are 5 cm, 12 cm and 13 cm? (correct to one decimal place)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sides of the triangle = 5cm, 12cm and 13 cm

**Formula used:**

Area of triangle = √s(s – a)(s – b) (s – c)

Semi perimeter (s) = (a + b + c)/2

Area of right angle triangle = 1/2 × base × height

**Concept used:**

Any triangle have three altitude, each altitude is from vertex to the opposite side.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2e9cf1388e1480090f530439838c728f3ea3625d8c40957c9d8f929d77db5c96.png] 

The semi perimeter of triangle = (5 + 12 + 13)/2

⇒ (30/2)

⇒ 15 cm

Area of triangle = √s(s – a)(s – b) (s – c)

⇒ √15(15 – 5)(15 – 12)(15 – 13)

⇒ √15 × 10 × 3 × 2

⇒ √900

⇒ 30 cm²

As we know 5, 12 and 13 are triplets and form a right angle triangle.

The smallest altitude will be on Hypotenuse

Area of right angle triangle = 1/2 × base × height

⇒ 30 = 1/2 × 13 × height

⇒ 60 = 13 × height

⇒ height = (60/13)

⇒ height = 4.6 cm

**∴ The length of the smallest altitude of the triangle is 4.6 cm**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2e9cf1388e1480090f530439838c728f3ea3625d8c40957c9d8f929d77db5c96.png] 

The length of smallest altitude is always perpendicular to the largest side of the triangle

So BO is the smallest altitude 

Now, BO = (AB × BC)/AC

⇒ BO = (5 × 12)/13 = 60/13 = 4.6 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 4.6 cm**

questions.question:
What is the difference in area (in cm²) of ΔABC having sides of 10 cm, 20 cm and 20 cm, and a right angled triangle ΔPQR with hypotenuse of 13 cm and one of the perpendiculars of 12 cm?

Note: √2 = 1.41, √3 = 1.73, √7 = 2.65, √13 = 3.61, √15 = 3.87, √21 = 4.58
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of ΔABC = (10 ÷ 4) × √(4 × 20² − 10²) = 2.5 × √1500 = 25√15 cm²

⇒ Area of ΔABC = 25 × 3.87 = 96.75 cm²

Base of right ΔPQR = √(13² − 12²) = 5 cm

⇒ Area of ΔPQR = &frac{1}{2} × 12 × 5 = 30 cm²

⇒ Difference in area = 96.75 − 30 = 66.75 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 66.75 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sides of ΔABC are 10 cm, 20 cm, and 20 cm.

In ΔPQR, hypotenuse = 13 cm, one perpendicular side = 12 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Heron's Formula for Area = √(s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c))

Pythagorean Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

Area of right triangle = &frac{1}{2} × Base × Height

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/76daef287940965b19fbefe3f121b47d7ec405e8ee74ab5678dbaee41007c21a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Semi-perimeter of ΔABC, s = (10 + 20 + 20) ÷ 2 = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 cm

⇒ Area of ΔABC = √(25 × (25 − 10) × (25 − 20) × (25 − 20))

⇒ Area of ΔABC = √(25 × 15 × 5 × 5) = √(9375) = 25√15 cm²

⇒ Given √15 ≈ 3.87, Area = 25 × 3.87 = 96.75 cm²

⇒ In right ΔPQR, Base = √(13² − 12²) = √(169 − 144) = √25 = 5 cm

⇒ Area of ΔPQR = &frac{1}{2} × 12 × 5 = 30 cm²

⇒ Difference in area = 96.75 − 30 = 66.75 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 66.75 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Heron's Formula

Used to find the area of a general triangle when all three sides are known: Area = √(s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)), where s = (a+b+c) ÷ 2.

Pythagorean Theorem

For any right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of squares of perpendicular and base: H² = P² + B².

Area of an Isosceles Triangle

Can also be calculated using the direct formula: Area = (b ÷ 4) × √(4a² − b²), where 'a' is the length of equal sides and 'b' is the base.
</p

questions.question: In ∆EFG, XY ∥ FG, area of the quadrilateral XFGY = 44 m2. If EX : XF = 2 : 3, then find the area of ∆EXY (in m2).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In ∆EFG, XY ∥ FG, area of the quadrilateral XFGY = 44 m².

EX : XF = 2 : 3

**Formula Used:**

Area of ∆EXY = (EX/EF)² × Area of ∆EFG

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c6bf315cecb9d76a639a05133c3e959cdb819fdb3a254644e4726280aaf3b589.png] 

Let EF = EX + XF

Let EX = 2k and XF = 3k

Then, EF = 2k + 3k = 5k

Ratio of EX to EF = EX/EF = 2k/5k = 2/5

Since XY ∥ FG, ∆EXY ~ ∆EFG (similar triangles)

Area of ∆EFG = Area of ∆EXY + Area of quadrilateral XFGY

Area of ∆EFG = Area of ∆EXY + 44

Ratio of areas of similar triangles = (Ratio of corresponding sides)²

Therefore, (Area of ∆EXY) / (Area of ∆EFG) = (EX/EF)²

(Area of ∆EXY) / (Area of ∆EFG) = (2/5)²

(Area of ∆EXY) / (Area of ∆EFG) = 4/25

Let Area of ∆EFG = A

Then, Area of ∆EXY = (4/25) × A

A = (4/25) × A + 44

⇒ A - (4/25) × A = 44

⇒ (21/25) × A = 44

⇒ A = 44 × (25/21)

⇒ A = 52.38

Area of ∆EXY = (4/25) × 52.38

⇒ Area of ∆EXY = 8.38 m²

**The area of ∆EXY is 8.38 m².**

questions.question: What is the perimeter (in cm, rounded off to one decimal place) of the sector of a circle with a radius of 10 cm and of angle 30º? (Use π = 3.14)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Perimeter of a sector = Radius × [θ × (π / 180) + 2]

⇒ Perimeter = 10 × [30 × (3.14 / 180) + 2]

⇒ Perimeter = 10 × [3.14 / 6 + 2]

⇒ Perimeter = 10 × [0.5233 + 2] = 10 × 2.5233

⇒ Perimeter = 25.233 cm ≈ 25.2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 25.2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the sector (r) = 10 cm

Angle of the sector (θ) = 30°

π = 3.14

**Formula Used:**

Length of Arc (l) = (θ / 360°) × 2πr

Perimeter of Sector = Length of Arc + 2 × Radius

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c5c5e56e034540190815f5f4a22ae0f57049b4aff84bdc485d8eaaba1f612bc6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Length of Arc (l) = (30° / 360°) × 2 × 3.14 × 10

⇒ l = (1 / 12) × 62.8

⇒ l = 5.233 cm

⇒ Perimeter of the sector = l + 2r

⇒ Perimeter = 5.233 + 2 × 10

⇒ Perimeter = 5.233 + 20

⇒ Perimeter = 25.233 cm

⇒ Rounding off to one decimal place, we get 25.2 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 25.2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Sector

The area of a sector of a circle is calculated using the formula: Area = (θ / 360°) × πr².

Length of an Arc

The length of the curved arc boundary of a sector can be found using: Arc Length = (θ / 360°) × 2πr.

Area of a Segment

The area of a segment is obtained by subtracting the area of the triangle formed by the radii and the chord from the area of the corresponding sector.
</p

questions.question: One-quarter of a circular pizza of radius 21 cm was removed from the whole pizza. What is the perimeter (in cm) of the remaining pizza? (Use π = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When 1/4 of a circular pizza is removed, the remaining shape consists of 3/4 of the original circumference plus two straight edges equal to the radius.

Perimeter = (3/4) × 2πr + 2r

Perimeter = (3/4) × 2 × (22/7) × 21 + (2 × 21)

Perimeter = 99 + 42 = 141 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 141 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b438551a0cf2fa7575c9c2e320edae4bef12707c96d94c48df3c58a1dee4f756.png] 

**Given:**

Radius of the circular pizza (r) = 21 cm

Part removed = 1/4 of the pizza

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of remaining shape = Length of remaining arc + 2 × Radius

Length of arc = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr

**Calculations:**

⇒ Angle of the remaining pizza (θ) = 360° − (1/4 × 360°) = 270°

⇒ Length of remaining arc = (270° ÷ 360°) × 2 × (22/7) × 21

⇒ Length of remaining arc = (3/4) × 2 × 22 × 3

⇒ Length of remaining arc = (3/4) × 132 = 99 cm

⇒ Total straight edges = 2 × Radius = 2 × 21 = 42 cm

⇒ Perimeter of remaining pizza = 99 + 42 = 141 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 141 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of a Semicircle

A semicircle's perimeter includes half the circumference and the full straight diameter: P = πr + 2r = r(π + 2).

Length of an Arc

The length of an arc is proportional to its central angle θ: Arc Length = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr.

Area of a Sector

The area of a sector with central angle θ is a fraction of the total area: Area = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr².
</p

questions.question: The altitude AD of a triangle ABC is 9 cm. If AB = 6√3 cm and CD = 3√3 cm, then what will be the measure of ∠A?

Here, Height = 9 = 6√3 × √3/2 

a = 6√3, so Height = a√3/2.

∴ Given triangle is an equilateral triangle.

So, ∠A = 60°.

**Traditional method:**

**Concept:**

Pythagoras theorem:

(AB)² = (BD)² + (AD)²

Equilateral Triangle:

AB = BC = AC

∠A = ∠B = ∠C = 60°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/72943c7a7cc57c87bf11f15066dd590009dc151a5656d00057d45a4297a06723.png] 

(6√3)² = (BD)² + 9²

⇒ BD = 3√3 cm 

∵ DC = BD = 3√3 cm

∴ BC = AC = AB = 6√3 cm &

**∠A = ∠B = ∠C = 60°**

**∴ ABC is an equilateral triangle.**

questions.question: The sides of a triangular park are in the ratio of 12 : 17 : 25 and its perimeter is 1080 m. The area (in hectares) of the park is ______.
questions.solution:
Ratio of sides of the triangle = 12x : 17x : 25x

Perimeter of the triangle = 1080

According to the question

12x + 17x + 25x = 1080

54x = 1080

x = 1080/54 = 20

Side of the triangle are = 12 × 20 = 240, 17 × 20 = 340 and 25 × 20 = 500

S = (240 + 340 + 500) /2 = 1080/2 = 540

Area of the triangle = √[s (s – a) (s – b) (s – c)]

√[540 (540 – 240) (540 – 340) (540 – 500)]

√[540 × 300 × 200 × 40] = 36000 m²

As we know,

10000 m² = 1 hectares

36000 m² = 3.6 hectares

A gear 15 cm in diameter is turning a gear 21 cm in diameter.

When the smaller gear has 105 revolutions, how many has the larger one made?

The number of revolutions is inversely proportional to the diameter of the gears.

**Calculation:**

Let the number of revolutions of the larger gear be x.

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**

questions.question: An arc on a circle that is 15 cm long subtends a 24° angle at the centre. What is the circumference of the circle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The total circumference of a circle corresponds to a central angle of 360°.

An angle of 24° corresponds to an arc length of 15 cm.

Therefore, the full 360° corresponds to: (360° ÷ 24°) × 15 cm.

Circumference = 15 × 15 = 225 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 225 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of arc (l) = 15 cm

Angle subtended at the centre (θ) = 24°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a8f42db93cf91cbfad75b638fd0649cbc68de09360c22a4771aee208e3c189a8.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Length of an arc = (θ ÷ 360°) × Circumference

**Calculations:**

⇒ 15 = (24° ÷ 360°) × Circumference

⇒ 15 = (1 ÷ 15) × Circumference

⇒ Circumference = 15 × 15

⇒ Circumference = 225 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 225 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Sector

The area of a sector of a circle with radius r and central angle θ is given by Area = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr².

Circumference of a Circle

The total boundary length of a circle is calculated as C = 2πr or C = πd, which corresponds to the full 360° arc.

Radian Measure

When measuring angles in radians, the formula for arc length is simplified to l = r × θ. A complete circle is 2π radians.
</p

questions.question: The radii of the two concentric circles are 27 cm and 18 cm. The area (in cm²) of the closed figure bounded by the boundaries of the circle is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of a circular ring = π × (R − r) × (R + r)

Substitute R = 27 and r = 18 into the formula:

⇒ Area = π × (27 − 18) × (27 + 18)

⇒ Area = π × 9 × 45

⇒ Area = 405π

**∴ The correct answer is 405π cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Outer radius of the circle (R) = 27 cm

⇒ Inner radius of the circle (r) = 18 cm

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Area of the bounded region (Ring) = Area of outer circle − Area of inner circle

⇒ Area = πR² − πr² = π(R² − r²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7c73cfae67109021ad082c3e0fe1844f1b58261101cc8bbd354f6f05c1b8cd46.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = π × (27)² − π × (18)²

⇒ Area = π × (729 − 324)

⇒ Area = 405π

**∴ The correct answer is 405π cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Concentric Circles

Concentric circles are circles that share the exact same center point but have different radii. The region enclosed between two concentric circles is often referred to as an annulus or a circular ring.

Width of the Circular Ring

The thickness or width of the ring is uniformly distributed and can be calculated by subtracting the inner radius from the outer radius: Width = R − r.

Algebraic Identities

When solving questions involving the difference of squares, applying the algebraic identity a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) will severely reduce the calculation time and prevent squaring large values.
</p

questions.question: A race track is in the shape of a ring whose inner and outer circumferences are 880 m and 1012 m, respectively. What is the area (in m²) of the track? (Take π = frac{{22}}{7})
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The inner circumferences = 880 m

The outer circumferences = 1012

**Formula used:**

The circumferences of a circle = 2 × π × Radius

The area of a circle = π × (Radius)²

**Calculation:**

Let, inner radius = r and Outer radius = R

So, 2 × (22/7) × r = 880 ⇒ r = 880 × (7/22) × (1/2) = 140 m

Also, 2 × (22/7) × R = 1012 ⇒ R = 1012 × (7/22) × (1/2) = 161 m

The area of the track = [(22/7) × (161)²] - [(22/7) × (140)²]

= (22/7) (25921 - 19600)

= (22/7) × 6321

= 19866 m2

**∴ The area (in m2) of the track is 19866 m2**
